author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 여름철새 수천 마리 · 나그네새 수백 마리 · 겨울철새 수십 마리
summary: 국내에서는 흔한 나그네새이자 흔한 여름철새이며, 남부에서는 드물게 겨울을 나기도 한다. 봄과 가을이면 전국의 강가·호숫가·바닷가에 내려앉아 혼자 지내거나 작은 무리를 이룬다. 날개를 몸 아래로 내린 채 빠른 날갯짓을 되풀이하며 땅이나 물가를 따라 낮게 나는 모습이 다른 도요류와 다르다. 북반구 북부에서 북극권까지 널리 분포하고, 동남아시아·호주·아프리카까지 내려가 겨울을 난다.

points.en: straight bill about as long as the head
greenish-brown upperparts, back and wing coverts edged blackish-brown
white wedge reaching up in front of the folded wing
rump the same colour as the back

young: 어린새는 겨울깃 어른새와 비슷하나 윗면, 특히 날개덮깃과 셋째날개깃의 깃 가장자리가 담황색이어서 가로무늬가 더 뚜렷하다.

similar.how: 삑삑도요는 날 때 허리가 희고 날개띠가 없으며, 가슴의 어두운 부분이 띠처럼 이어지고 접은 날개 앞으로 흰색이 올라오지 않는다.

art.subject: Common Sandpiper (Actitis hypoleucos), adult as seen on Korean riversides from April to September: crown, hindneck and upperparts greenish olive-brown, the back, scapulars and wing coverts finely marked with dark brown bars and edges; a short whitish supercilium and white eye-ring above a dark brown eye-stripe; sides of the breast grey-brown with fine streaks, forming two patches almost meeting in the centre; underparts clean white, the white reaching up as a sharp wedge between the breast patch and the bend of the folded wing; tail olive-brown with white-barred outer edges. Bill dark brown, paler at the base; dark eye; legs dull greyish-green to yellowish-olive.
art.pose: flying low over the water on down-held wings with rapid, flickering wingbeats
art.scene: Korean riverside in spring: pebbly bank beside shallow flowing water; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing: straight bill about head length, olive-brown upperparts with fine dark edging, short pale supercilium and white eye-ring, streaked brown breast-side patch, white wedge rising in front of the folded wing, tail projecting beyond the wingtips
adult in flight seen from above: wings bowed downwards below the body, long bold white wing-bar, rump and central tail the same olive-brown as the back, white sides to the tail
art.build: Small, short-legged, horizontal sandpiper, 20cm, noticeably larger than a sparrow; short neck, crouched stance, and a long tail that projects clearly beyond the wingtips at rest. Constantly bobs its rear and tail up and down. Bill straight, about as long as the head. Legs short, greyish-green. In flight it skims low over the water with stiff, shallow, flickering wingbeats on down-bowed wings, interspersed with short glides; a bold white wing-bar runs along the whole wing; rump and centre of the tail brown like the back, tail sides white.
avoid: Do not paint a white rump; the rump is as brown as the back (Green and Wood Sandpipers have white rumps).
Do not let the wingtips reach the tail tip; the tail clearly extends beyond the folded wings.
Do not paint bold white spots on the upperparts (Wood Sandpiper) or long yellow legs.
Do not paint a uniform streaked band across the whole breast; the brown sits on the breast sides, with white pushing up in front of the wing.
